area: the server — disconnecting what nothing asks for any more
status: DEPLOYED 2026-09-02 on founder instruction. Formal release gate still unmet (qa_all_green false).
approved_by: aveenswamy1989@gmail.com (founder) — "first i want to clean up all things what we agreed... so as per that we complete 3 and 4 passes", 2026-09-02
mockup_source: NONE. This pass has no user interface at all — it removes server code that nothing calls.
impact_review_note: The founder authored the cleaning plan and explicitly asked for passes 3 and 4 to be completed.
what_this_pass_is: Delete the server code for everything removed in pass 1, now that nothing asks for it. The DATA is deliberately untouched — that is pass 4, kept separate because it is the only irreversible step.
removed: Seven route files and seven controllers, plus their mounts and two stragglers wired directly into admin and brand routes: agencies, referrals (public and admin), enquiries, meals, the pre-agreement handshake, and creator lookbooks. 2,224 lines. The clients' last doors went with them — mealsApi and the handshake bindings on both phone and website, plus the orphaned dish-group and lookbook calls.
the_ordering_was_the_whole_point: Every endpoint was re-checked for callers in BOTH the phone apps AND the website before removal — a check that only became meaningful once the website was cleaned. An hour before this commit the website still called 19 meals endpoints, 16 referral endpoints and 7 handshake endpoints. This exact change would have broken the live site. That is the outside-in rule (screens, then engine, then memory) doing its job, after I had nearly broken it myself by leaving the website out of pass 1.

verification.the_server_loads: Not a parse check. `require('./src/app.js')` resolves the ENTIRE application — every route file, every controller, and every service they pull in. If any of the 14 deleted files were still referenced anywhere, that throws. It does not.
verification.endpoints_confirmed_gone_in_production: GET /v1/agencies/me, /v1/meals/settings and /v1/referrals/settings all return 404 after the deploy, where they previously answered.
verification.honest_limit_on_two_of_them: /v1/brands/me/collab-requests and /v1/follower/enquiry still answer 401, and that is NOT evidence they survive. Those prefixes apply authentication at the router level, before route matching — a path that has never existed (/v1/brands/me/this-never-existed) returns 401 too. The probe cannot distinguish there. The real evidence is that the source contains no such route and the whole app loads without the files.
verification.a_mid_rollout_false_alarm: The first probe showed /v1/agencies/me still answering 401 while /v1/meals/settings already returned 404 — Render was mid-rollout. Re-probed rather than concluding the removal had failed, per the standing rule to probe twice.

deployed_2026_09_02.vercel: Redeployed — CDN cache reset to Age: 0.
deployed_2026_09_02.note: The influencer bundle carries the negotiation door as well as this pass. Flagged to the founder before publishing rather than shipped quietly.

release.deploy_class: PRODUCTION-IMPACTING. backend/src changed; endpoints that previously answered now return 404.
release.outward_facing: Only to anything still calling the removed endpoints — which, after the website cleanup, is nothing. A phone that has not opened since before pass 1 still holds old JavaScript that would call them; it picks up the new bundle on next launch, and every removed feature held zero real data.
release.why_not_released: gov-check Rule 2 refuses released:true while qa_all_green is false.
release.device_walk_required: Light. Open each app once and confirm it still works; the removed features have no screens left to visit.

next: Pass 4 — erase the data. The only irreversible pass. Everything holding real rows is exported to a file BEFORE it is dropped, so a reversed decision stays recoverable even though the code is gone.
